the development of novel antibody drug conjugates (ADCS) for the treatment of HER2 positive breast cancers.

deBougin is a novel and potent cytotoxic protein that can be conjugated to antibodies and is unaffected by mechanisms that lead to resistance against anti-microtuble ADCs.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have identified a novel mechanism of action for ADCs and have demonstrated that deBougin is effective against resistance mechanisms selected in tumor cells in response to ADC therapy.
deBougin is a promising ADC payload with a novel mechanism of action that can overcome drug resistance to other ADCs.
deBouginin is an effective payload to overcome resistance mechanisms selected in tumors that survive treatment with anti-microtuble ADCs.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the mechanism of action of a deBouganine-based ADC is distinct from the mechanism of action for ADCs based on anti-microtubleule agents.
deBougin, a de-immunization variant of bouganins, is an effective payload for ADCs and is unaffected by the resistance mechanism of MDR1 and MRP1 efflux pumps.
ADCs composed of RIP payloads are unaffected by resistance mechanisms that affect ADCs composed of microtubule targeting agents.
